newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan mooncake pyramid takes the biscuit.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan mooncake pyramid takes the biscuit.

text.p: Residents of southern Taiwan have built a 73-layer, three-metre (10 ft) high mooncake pyramid to celebrate the mid-autumn festival, the mass circulation China Times newspaper reported on Sunday.
Organisers used some 25,000 moon cakes, costing T$500,000 (US$18,500), to build the pyramid, it said.
The mooncakes, sweet pastries made of lotus seed paste, would be given free of charge to residents in southern county of Kaohsiung on the day of the festival, which falls on September 27.
Mooncakes are eaten at the mid-autumn festival to commemorate the practice of hiding messages in cakes to overthrow the Mongol emperors in 14th century China.
